source.title: https://www.crossfit.com/essentials/the-clean-and-jerk
source.locator: Split jerk uses rapid dip-drive, split receiving footwork and overhead stabilization; CrossFit describes high technical demands plus flexibility, coordination and balance.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/body-part/abs/
source.locator: Dynamic floor abdominal work is supported and stable; alternating sprinter-style limb action adds trunk control and coordination beyond a basic crunch.

source.publisher: ACE Exercise Library — running and integrated lower-body drills
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/body-part/legs-thighs/hamstrings/
source.locator: Explosive running drills require repeated single-leg support, rapid lower-limb cycling and high force production.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/135/bodyweight-squat/
source.locator: ACE classifies the bodyweight squat as beginner and specifies controlled hip/knee motion, heel contact and knee/foot alignment.

source.publisher: Front Squat to Overhead Press / advanced integrated exercise family
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/experience/advanced/
source.locator: ACE lists front-squat-to-overhead-press patterns as advanced integrated work, combining squat mobility with coordinated overhead drive.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/experience/advanced/
source.locator: Squat-thrust/burpee-family transitions combine squat, plank support and rapid position changes, increasing whole-body coordination and strength demand.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/stability-ball/
source.locator: ACE stability-ball core work uses an unstable support surface; abdominal flexion remains moderate in strength and technique demand.

source.publisher: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl / Glute Bridge
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/stability-ball/
source.locator: ACE lists stability-ball glute bridge and hamstring curl as intermediate, combining hip extension, knee flexion and ball control.

source.publisher: Stability Ball Knee Tucks / advanced stability-ball core family
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/stability-ball/
source.locator: ACE classifies stability-ball knee-tuck patterns as advanced; plank support plus ball travel raises trunk strength and control demand.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/61/stability-ball-pikes/
source.locator: ACE classifies the pike as advanced and requires a rigid plank progressing to an inverted hip-flexed position with extended limbs on the ball.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/stability-ball/
source.locator: ACE classifies stability-ball reverse extensions as advanced, reflecting substantial posterior-chain control on an unstable surface.

source.publisher: Stability Ball Prone Walkout / rollout family
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/stability-ball/
source.locator: ACE stability-ball walkout/rollout-family work requires sustained trunk stiffness while the support point moves away from the body.

source.publisher: Step-up and Biceps Curl exercise families
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/28/step-up/
source.locator: Combining repeated step-up mechanics with a curl adds dual-task coordination; the step-up itself is beginner-level with controlled single-leg loading.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/barbell/
source.locator: ACE lists barbell biceps curl as intermediate; standing bilateral curling has limited balance and mobility demands but requires controlled elbow mechanics.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/body-part/butt-hips/
source.locator: Standing unilateral hip-extension patterns require stance-leg stabilization and controlled hip motion against resistance.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/bench/
source.locator: ACE pullover patterns use controlled shoulder extension/flexion through a substantial arc; standing cable execution adds modest postural control.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/weight-machines-selectorized/
source.locator: ACE lists machine calf raise as beginner; machine support minimizes balance while ankle plantarflexion is simple and constrained.

records.exerciseName: Standing Chest and Anterior Shoulder Stretch

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/209/standing-chest-stretch/
source.locator: ACE classifies standing chest stretch as beginner and describes shoulder external rotation/retraction with optional anterior-deltoid stretch; strength demand is minimal.

source.publisher: Forward Linear Jumps / jump training family
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/no-equipment/
source.locator: ACE jump drills emphasize coordinated takeoff and landing with lower-body triple extension, supporting moderate balance, mobility and strength requirements.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/
source.locator: Standing side-bending stretch is a low-load mobility drill; the primary demand is controlled lateral trunk range rather than strength or skill.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/117/bosu-sup-reg-sup-squat-jumps/
source.locator: ACE BOSU squat-jump instruction stresses balance support, landing control and prior mastery of regular squats; static BOSU squatting retains elevated stability/technical demand.

source.publisher: ACE Ab Exercise Library — standing trunk rotations
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/body-part/abs/
source.locator: ACE explicitly includes standing trunk rotations in its abdominal exercise collection; unloaded rotation is primarily a controlled mobility pattern with low strength demand.

source.publisher: ACE Exercise Library — beginner stretch family
source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/experience/beginner/
source.locator: Standing overhead triceps stretching is a supported low-load mobility pattern; primary demand is shoulder/elbow range rather than strength or coordination.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/body-part/legs-thighs/hamstrings/
source.locator: Unilateral standing knee flexion requires stance-leg stabilization while the moving leg performs a simple hamstring curl through controlled range.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/equipment/no-equipment/
source.locator: ACE jump drills require coordinated takeoff/landing and explosive lower-body extension; star-jump limb abduction adds whole-body coordination.

source.title: https://www.acefitness.org/resources/everyone/exercise-library/94/forward-lunge/
source.locator: ACE rates forward lunge intermediate and explicitly requires single-leg stabilization, controlled hip/knee lowering and alignment; dumbbells preserve these demands.
